extracted.intended_audience: policy officials, analysts, and government agencies preparing or seeking Regulatory Impact Assessments (RIAs) in New Zealand
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and expectations for preparing Regulatory Impact Assessments (RIAs) and related impact statements to inform Cabinet decisions on proposals to create, change or repeal legislation or regulations in New Zealand. Includes what RIAs must summarise and when they are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of a Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: RIAs summarise analysis produced for the purpose of informing Cabinet decisions on proposals to create, change or repeal legislation or regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIAs are prepared by the responsible government agency to support Cabinet decision‑making. Many documents on the page are described as 'relating to analysis produced for the purpose of informing Cabinet decisions' or 'to support final Cabinet decisions'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarise the problem that needs to be addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: The RIA must set out the problem that needs to be addressed by the proposed legislative or regulatory change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly define the policy problem or deficiency motivating the proposal so that options and impacts can be assessed against that problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify options for addressing the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: RIAs must present options for addressing the problem (including the status quo and viable alternatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options should be set out explicitly so Cabinet can compare different approaches; many listed RIAs analyse multiple options as part of decision support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess the costs and benefits of each option
rubrics_metrics.description: RIAs must analyse the costs and benefits of each option considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative and qualitative assessment where possible. Where proposals involve fees or cost recovery, prepare a Regulatory and Cost Recovery Impact Statement (RCRIS/CRIS) that specifically considers cost recovery implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document who has been consulted and their views
rubrics_metrics.description: RIAs must summarise who has been consulted in developing the proposal and what views were expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record stakeholder engagement and reflect how consultation feedback influenced option design or assessment. The page repeatedly lists 'who has been consulted and their views' as a required RIA element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals for implementation and review
rubrics_metrics.description: RIAs should include proposals for how the preferred option would be implemented and how it would be reviewed over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out implementation steps, responsibilities, timelines, and any evaluation or review mechanisms to assess effectiveness post‑implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: When RIAs must be provided and published
rubrics_metrics.description: An RIA is required when there is a proposal to create, change or repeal legislation or regulations; RIAs are published when the relevant Bill is introduced, the regulation is gazetted, or at ministerial release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should prepare RIAs for Cabinet consideration and plan publication timing to coincide with Bill introduction, gazetting of regulations, or ministerial release so the public record and Cabinet papers align. The page links to Treasury's full list of RIAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the appropriate impact statement type (RIS, RIA, IRIS, RCRIS/CRIS, Supplementary Analysis, Interim RIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different kinds of impact analysis documents are used depending on purpose: Regulatory Impact Statement (RIS), Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA), Interim Regulatory Impact Statement (IRIS), Regulatory and Cost Recovery Impact Statement (RCRIS/CRIS), Supplementary Analysis Report, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the form that matches the proposal and analytic needs (for example, RCRIS/CRIS when considering fee increases or cost recovery; IRIS for approvals to release consultation documents). The page provides many examples and labels showing how different documents are used to support Cabinet decisions.
